front.title: Framework and YANG Data Model for the Network Management Agent (NMA) A2U Interface

postal.street: Building A01, 1600 Yuhangtang Road, Wuchang Street, Yuhang District

abstract.t: This document defines a standardized northbound interface for the Network Management Agent (NMA) to expose its capabilities to upper-layer systems (OSS/BSS), namely the A2U (Agent-to-User) interface. The document includes an architectural framework, information model, interface primitives, and transport bindings. The information model is defined using YANG, covering five core components: agent capability discovery, unified intent submission, task lifecycle management, human-in-the-loop confirmation, and event notification. The interface primitives are implemented based on HTTP + JSON + SSE, supporting dual-modal input of natural language and structured data, and sharing a unified task state machine and event streaming mechanism. This document aims to provide an interoperable standardized foundation for upper-layer systems to invoke NMA capabilities.

section.title: Background
section.t: As telecom networks continue to scale, traditional manual configuration and fixed API-based operation and maintenance models can no longer meet the demands for efficient operations. The Network Management Agent (NMA) is an autonomous entity with perception, decision-making, and execution capabilities. Operators and vendors are accelerating research, development, and deployment of NMAs to drive Autonomous Networks (AN) toward Level 4 (L4).

Currently, defines the A2U interface exposed by the NMA upward. This interface serves as a critical interface for upper-layer orchestrators or OSS/BSS systems to invoke lower-layer vendor NMA capabilities, and urgently requires standardized definition to enable upper-layer systems to discover, invoke, and manage NMA capabilities in a uniform manner, thereby enabling autonomous network management tasks.

section.title: Document Scope
section.t: This document defines the NMA A2U (Agent-to-User) interface, specifying the interaction between upper-layer systems (N+1 layer Controller/User/OSS/BSS) and the NMA. Specifically, it includes:

ul.li: Architectural principles and interface positioning ();
Information model (), defined using YANG ;
Interface primitives and protocol details ();
Transport binding requirements ();
Relationship with existing standards ().

section.title: Non-Goals
section.t: The following topics are out of scope for this document and will be defined in subsequent independent documents:

li.t: A2A (Agent-to-Agent) peer collaboration interface: Peer negotiation mechanisms between NMAs across domains belong to future work;

ul.li: Domain-specific constraints: Specific constraint conditions and information model extensions for domains such as OTN service provisioning, IP fault handling, and wireless energy saving are not defined in this document. This document only provides the anydata extension mechanism;

li.t: Specific LLM model specifications: Implementation details of intent parsing engines (LLM, rule-based, or hybrid) are outside the scope of this document.

section.title: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: The interface through which the NMA exposes capabilities to upper-layer systems (N+1 layer controller, OSS/BSS, human operators, etc.). Upper-layer systems are always in the Client/User role at the protocol level and do not constitute a peer Agent relationship with the NMA.

See . An autonomous entity deployed within a network management domain, equipped with intent parsing, task planning, tool invocation, result feedback, and human-in-the-loop collaboration capabilities.
A goal description submitted by a user or upper-layer system to the NMA, expressible via natural language or structured data.
A management operation unit instantiated and executed by the NMA for a specific Intent, with a complete lifecycle, execution plan, and audit trail.
A sequence of steps generated by the NMA to complete a Task, where each step corresponds to a specific tool/interface invocation.
A pending resolution interaction unit generated by the NMA when it determines that an operation requires review by a human or upper-layer system.
A state change notification pushed by the NMA to subscribers, covering the full lifecycle nodes including intent receipt, parsing, plan generation, step execution, and task completion.
The return structure for NMA capability discovery, describing the NMA identifier, version, skill list, interface endpoints, and autonomy policies.
The AN L0-L5 levels defined by TMF IG1230, used to declare the maximum autonomy capability of an NMA for a specific skill.
An HTTP-based server push technology with media type text/event-stream.

section.title: Roles and Interface Positioning
section.t: The A2U interface involves two roles:

li.t: NMA: The server side of the interface, responsible for receiving intents, parsing, planning, executing, and returning results;

Upper-Layer System: The client side of the interface, including OSS, BSS, orchestrators, or human operation terminals. Regardless of whether it has internal Agent capabilities, it is in the User role at the A2U protocol level.

section.t: The A2U interface is physically deployed northbound of the Controller or NMA gateway, as an extension plane of the existing RESTCONF/HTTP NBI, rather than an independent port or protocol stack.

section.title: Design Principles
section.t: The A2U interface follows four design principles:

dl.dd: Sharing the Controller's 443 port, TLS, and authentication infrastructure, but logically isolating /restconf/* (configuration plane) from /nma/* (Agent plane) to avoid interference between routine management traffic and agent traffic.
All interactions are based on HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 + JSON, without enforcing RESTCONF encoding rules, lowering the integration threshold for upper-layer systems.
The information model uses YANG definitions, aligned with existing YANG automation standards such as ; transport binding uses native HTTP + JSON.
Human operators and machine OSS invoke the same /nma/intent endpoint, differentiated by the mode field, sharing the subsequent Task lifecycle and Event mechanism.

section.title: Interaction Modes
section.t: The A2U interface supports three interaction modes:

li.t: Request-Response Mode: For structured intent submission, task query, capability discovery, and other immediate operations;
SSE Streaming Mode: For natural language dialogue, task status streaming push, and long-duration task execution monitoring;

Confirmation Closed-Loop Mode: When the NMA determines that operation risk exceeds the current autonomy level, it pauses execution and pushes a Confirmation to the upper layer, waiting for an explicit resolution before continuing or terminating.

section.title: YANG Module Overview
section.t: This document defines the following six YANG modules:

table.name: YANG Modules Defined in This Document

tr.td: Task lifecycle, plan, result, audit log

section.t: Module dependency: ietf-nma-a2u-common is the base module; the other five modules all reference its definitions.

section.title: Common Types (ietf-nma-a2u-common)
section.t: This module defines the base types and groupings shared by all modules in this document.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-common
figure.artwork:
module: ietf-nma-a2u-common +--u submitter-info
typedefs: +-- autonomy-level +-- intent-mode +-- intent-type +-- task-state +-- confirmation-type +-- nma-a2u-event-type

section.t: Key type definitions:

ul.li: autonomy-level: Enumeration from L0 to L5, corresponding to TMF AN levels;
intent-mode: Enumeration of natural-language and structured;
intent-type: Enumeration of CREATE, DELETE, MODIFY, QUERY, REPORT, DIAGNOSE;
task-state: Unified state machine: PENDING, ANALYZING, AWAITING_CLARIFICATION, PLANNING, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, EXECUTING, COMPLETED, FAILED, ABORTED;

event-type: intent-received, intent-parsed, intent-clarification-required, intent-rejected, plan-generated, confirmation-required, step-started, step-completed, step-failed, task-completed, task-failed, task-suspended;
confirmation-type: EXECUTION, PARAMETER_CHANGE, DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATION, POLICY_VIOLATION.

section.title: Agent Capability Model (ietf-nma-a2u-capabilities)
section.t: The information model for NMA capability discovery, corresponding to the GET /nma/agent-capabilities return structure.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-capabilities
figure.artwork: module: ietf-nma-a2u-capabilities +--ro agent-capabilities +--ro agent-id string +--ro version string +--ro skills* [skill-id] | +--ro skill-id string | +--ro name string | +--ro description? string | +--ro input-schema? union (yang-uri | anydata) | +--ro confirmation-required boolean | +--ro max-autonomy-level autonomy-level | +--ro tags* string +--ro endpoints* [name] | +--ro name string | +--ro uri inet:uri | +--ro methods* string +--ro policies +--ro default-autonomy-level? autonomy-level +--ro human-in-the-loop? boolean +--ro max-timeout-seconds? uint32

section.t: Key semantics:

ul.li: input-schema: Can reference an external domain YANG module URI (e.g., ietf-trans-client-service), or embed an anydata description;
confirmation-required: Declares whether this skill triggers the confirmation closed-loop by default;
max-autonomy-level: The highest autonomy level this skill can reach without human intervention.

section.title: Intent Model (ietf-nma-a2u-intent)
section.t: The unified intent model supporting dual-modal expression.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-intent
figure.artwork: module: ietf-nma-a2u-intent +--rw intents +--rw intent* [intent-id] +--rw intent-id string +--rw mode intent-mode +--rw submitter | +--rw type enumeration {user, system, agent} | +--rw id string +--rw timestamp yang:date-and-time +--rw state task-state +--rw task-id? -> /ietf-nma-a2u-tasks:tasks/task/task-id +--rw (mode-choice)? | +--:(natural-language) | | +--rw natural-language | | +--rw text string | | +--rw parsed-result? anydata | | +--rw confidence? decimal64 (0..1) | | +--rw parser? enumeration {llm, rule, hybrid} | +--:(structured) | +--rw structured | +--rw type intent-type | +--rw target-resource? string | +--rw constraints anydata | +--rw priority? uint8 (1..10) +--ro estimated-completion? uint32

section.t: Key design points:

ul.li: mode is a mandatory field determining the subsequent branch;
constraints is of type anydata, without built-in specific fields, to be filled by external domain YANG modules (e.g., ietf-trans-client-service) via augmentation or reference;
parsed-result is an internal backfill field by the NMA, parsing natural language into a structured intermediate representation for upper-layer auditing;

confidence: The NMA's confidence score for natural language parsing results, ranging from 0 to 1. A value of 1 indicates full confidence, while 0 indicates inability to parse. The upper-layer system can use this to decide whether to request clarification or resubmission;
parser: Identifies the parser type used internally by the NMA (LLM, rule-based, or hybrid), for upper-layer awareness of the parsing mechanism;
task-id establishes a one-to-one association between Intent and Task.

section.title: Task Model (ietf-nma-a2u-tasks)
section.t: The task lifecycle management model.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-tasks
figure.artwork: module: ietf-nma-a2u-tasks +--ro tasks +--ro task* [task-id] +--ro task-id string +--ro parent-intent-id -> /ietf-nma-a2u-intent:intents/intent/intent-id +--ro state task-state +--ro created-at yang:date-and-time +--ro updated-at yang:date-and-time +--ro plan* [step-id] | +--ro step-id string | +--ro action string | +--ro target? string | +--ro input-params? anydata | +--ro status enumeration {pending, running, completed, failed, skipped} | +--ro observation? string | +--ro started-at? yang:date-and-time | +--ro completed-at? yang:date-and-time +--ro result | +--ro success boolean | +--ro summary string | +--ro affected-resources* string | +--ro output-data? anydata +--ro audit-log* [log-id] +--ro log-id string +--ro timestamp yang:date-and-time +--ro actor string +--ro action string +--ro details? string

section.t: Key semantics:

ul.li: plan is the execution step sequence generated by the NMA, reflecting explainability;
observation records environmental feedback after each step execution, supporting reasoning patterns such as ReAct;
audit-log provides an immutable operation audit trail, meeting telecom-grade compliance requirements.

section.title: Confirmation Model (ietf-nma-a2u-confirmations)
section.t: The human-in-the-loop confirmation model.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-confirmations
figure.artwork: module: ietf-nma-a2u-confirmations +--rw confirmations +--rw confirmation* [confirmation-id] +--rw confirmation-id string +--rw task-id -> /ietf-nma-a2u-tasks:tasks/task/task-id +--rw type confirmation-type +--rw priority uint8 (1..10) +--rw timeout-seconds uint32 +--rw context anydata +--rw allowed-actions* enumeration {approve, reject, modify-and-approve, escalate-to-human} +--rw status enumeration {pending, approved, rejected, modified, expired, escalated} +--rw resolution +--rw action? enumeration +--rw modified-params? anydata +--rw resolved-by? string +--rw resolved-at? yang:date-and-time

section.t: Key semantics:

ul.li: context carries the display data for the Confirmation Card (e.g., before/after comparison, impact scope). The format is determined by the business scenario and can be extended by different domains or scenarios;
allowed-actions explicitly defines the resolution types available to the upper-layer system;
modify-and-approve allows the upper layer to modify parameters before approval, achieving flexible collaboration.

section.title: Event/Notification Model (ietf-nma-a2u-events)
section.t: The event notification model.

figure.title: Tree Diagram for ietf-nma-a2u-events
figure.artwork: module: ietf-nma-a2u-events +--ro events +--ro event* [event-id] +--ro event-id string +--ro event-type nma-a2u-event-type +--ro task-id -> /ietf-nma-a2u-tasks:tasks/task/task-id +--ro timestamp yang:date-and-time +--ro recipient? string +--ro payload +--ro (event-payload)? +--:(intent-receipt) | +--ro estimated-processing-time? uint32 | +--ro accepted boolean +--:(clarification-request) | +--ro missing-fields* string | +--ro ambiguous-fields* string | +--ro questions* string +--:(rejection) | +--ro reason-code string | +--ro explanation string +--:(plan-generated) | +--ro step-count uint32 | +--ro estimated-duration? uint32 +--:(confirmation-required) | +--ro confirmation-id -> /ietf-nma-a2u-confirmations:confirmations/confirmation/confirmation-id +--:(step-completed) | +--ro step-id string | +--ro observation? string +--:(step-failed) | +--ro step-id string | +--ro exception-type string | +--ro affected-scope? string | +--ro remedial-suggestions* string +--:(task-completed) | +--ro summary string | +--ro affected-resources* string +--:(task-failed) +--ro reason string +--ro failed-step-id? string

section.t: Key semantics:

ul.li: event-type: Same as defined in ;
recipient: Identifies the intended recipient of the event, supporting targeted push in multi-subscriber scenarios;

payload: Uses a choice structure to carry differentiated content based on event-type. clarification-request is used when the NMA requests supplementary information from the upper layer, rejection is used when the NMA rejects an inexecutable intent, step-failed is used to report step-level exceptions and suggested remediation measures, and task-completed is used to return the final task result summary;
All events are pushed via SSE or polling.

section.title: Overview
section.t: The A2U interface defines seven core primitives, all based on HTTP. Request and response bodies use JSON encoding, with schemas corresponding to the JSON mapping of the YANG modules in .

section.title: Discover
section.t: Retrieve the NMA capability card.

ul.li: Method: GET
URI: /nma/agent-capabilities
Response: 200 OK, body is an agent-capabilities instance (JSON)
Error codes: 401 Unauthorized, 500 Internal Server Error

section.title: Submit Intent
section.t: Unified intent submission entry, supporting dual-modal natural language and structured input.

ul.li: Method: POST
URI: /nma/intent
Synchronous scenario (simple query): 200 OK, body contains task and result;
Asynchronous scenario (complex operation): 202 Accepted, returns task-id and initial state;
SSE scenario: 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream, streaming return of Event sequence.
Error codes: 400 Bad Request (mode mismatch), 422 Unprocessable Content (parse failure), 401, 500

section.t: Key semantics: The same endpoint and subsequent mechanism, differentiated by mode. After the NMA internally parses NL into a structured intermediate representation, it enters the unified Task lifecycle.

section.title: Query Task
section.t: Query a single task status and complete history.

ul.li: Method: GET
URI: /nma/tasks/{task-id}
Response: 200 OK, body is a task instance (including plan, result, audit-log)
Error codes: 404 Not Found

section.title: List Tasks
section.t: List active or historical tasks.

ul.li: Method: GET
URI: /nma/tasks
state: Filter by status (optional, multi-value);
submitter-id: Filter by submitter (optional);
limit: Maximum number of returns (default 50, max 200);
offset: Pagination offset (optional).
Response: 200 OK, body is a task array and pagination metadata.

section.title: Subscribe Task Events
section.t: Subscribe to real-time event streams for a specified task.

ul.li: Method: GET
URI: /nma/tasks/{task-id}/events
Response: 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream

figure.artwork: event: <event-type> id: <event-id> data: <JSON payload>

ul.li: Error codes: 404

section.t: Note: The event stream can also be embedded in the SSE response of POST /nma/intent (see ). This endpoint provides independent subscription enhancement.

section.title: Confirm
section.t: Submit a confirmation resolution.

ul.li: Method: POST
URI: /nma/confirm
Response: 200 OK, returns updated task status; or 202 Accepted if the NMA needs to asynchronously process subsequent execution.
Error codes: 404 (confirmation-id does not exist), 409 Conflict (expired or already processed), 422 (modified parameter validation failure)

section.title: Abort
section.t: Forcibly terminate an executing task.

ul.li: Method: POST
URI: /nma/tasks/{task-id}/abort
Request Body: Optional reason field to explain the termination cause.
Response: 200 OK (terminated) or 409 Conflict (task already completed or failed, cannot be terminated).
Error codes: 404
Protocol version: HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 ;
Encoding: Request and response bodies MUST use JSON , character encoding UTF-8;
Media type: application/json;
URI design: Following Section , version control via URI prefix (e.g., /nma/v1/) or Accept-Version request header. This document does not mandate a version policy.
Media type: text/event-stream;

li.t: Applicable scenarios: Natural language dialogue flow, long-duration task status push, independent event subscription;

ul.li: Reconnection mechanism: When the client disconnects, the standard SSE reconnection mechanism applies; the NMA SHOULD support the Last-Event-ID header to achieve resumption;
Data format: data: line embedding JSON, structure corresponding to the ietf-nma-a2u-events module.

section.title: Relationship with RESTCONF
section.t: The A2U interface may physically share the Controller's 443 port and TLS session, but is logically isolated from the /restconf plane.
This document chooses native HTTP + JSON rather than RESTCONF binding, for the following reasons:

li.t: Streaming requirements: SSE is not fully compatible with the request-response model of RESTCONF;
Model-anchored, transport-decoupled: The information model still uses YANG definitions to ensure semantic rigor, but the transport binding remains lightweight.

section.t: NMA implementations MAY simultaneously expose RESTCONF bindings (e.g., via ), but this document only specifies the HTTP + JSON binding.

section.title: Relationship to Existing Standards

tr.td: NMA as L4 autonomy enhancement layer, reusing YANG modeling methods
Aligning Intent definition, extending dual-modal expression mechanism
constraints references external YANG via anydata or leafref

section.t: Boundary with A2A interfaces: When two NMAs collaborate across domains, they form a peer Agent relationship and should use A2A protocols (such as A2A-T or other standards defined subsequently). When an upper-layer OSS invokes an NMA, regardless of whether the OSS has internal Agent capabilities, it is in the A2U User role at the protocol level.

section.title: Future Work
section.t: This document only defines the NMA A2U basic framework and generic information model. The following work will be advanced in subsequent independent documents.

section.title: Domain-Specific Extension Approach
section.t: The constraints field in the A2U framework is designed as an anydata extension point, allowing various professional domains and operation scenarios to define specific constraints through independent YANG modules or JSON Schema.

Subsequent domain modules can access the basic framework through two approaches: First, YANG Augmentation, augmenting the constraints node of ietf-nma-a2u-intent to define domain-specific leaf nodes; Second, URI reference, referencing external YANG module URIs in the input-schema of agent-capabilities, with the NMA and upper-layer system parsing anydata content through an agreed schema.

section.title: Cross-Domain Collaboration (A2A Interface)
section.t: When NMAs need to collaborate across administrative domains (e.g., cross-operator, cross-IP/optical, cross-vendor), they form a peer Agent relationship, requiring standardization of Task delegation, result aggregation, capability negotiation, and mapping with existing multi-agent collaboration protocols such as A2A-T . This is outside the scope of this document.

The key distinction between the A2A interface and the A2U interface in this document is that the A2U User is always in the Client role, while both parties in A2A are peer Agent roles, requiring bidirectional intent submission, negotiation, and commitment mechanisms.
